Article Title: BJP announces month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to mark PM Modi’s 25 years in public service
Article Text:
BJP to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ nationwide to mark 25 years of PM Modi’s parliamentary political journey. (Photo: ANI)

Campaign to begin on PM Modi’s birthday

‘India is the fastest-growing major economy’

Nabin cites women-led development, border villages

‘Gujarat’s growth became a development model’

NEW DELHI: The BJP will launch a month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ on September 17 to mark PM Modi completing 25 years in public service, with programmes ranging from blood donation and cleanliness drives to exhibitions, seminars and welfare-scheme camps across the country.The campaign will continue until October 17. October 7 will mark 25 years since PM Modi took oath as Gujarat chief minister in 2001.Announcing the campaign at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Wednesday, party national president Nitin Nabin said, “Today, we have gathered here to discuss the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan'. On October 7, 2026, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi will complete 25 years of public service, a journey that began when he assumed office as the Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001. Over the past 25 years, he has steadfastly continued this journey of service, embracing the mantra of transitioning from public service to service of the nation. ”The campaign will start on September 17, PM Modi’s birthday, which the BJP observes as ‘Seva Diwas’.“We will begin the programme with a blood donation camp. On September 17, we will organise the 'Ashirwad Ka Diya' programme. On October 2, we will organise a cleanliness drive, as we do every year,” Nabin said.An inaugural programme titled ‘Ashirbadar Banti’ (Lamp of Blessings) will also be held on September 17.BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde has been appointed national convener of the campaign. A seven-member team comprising a minister, an organisational general secretary and five senior leaders will be formed in every state to coordinate the programmes.The party will hold photo and digital exhibitions tracing PM Modi’s 25-year political journey and focusing on his governance record, development initiatives and welfare schemes.Seminars and intellectual forums on good governance, development and Antyodaya are also planned, along with interactions with young people and other sections of society. Special camps will spread awareness about welfare schemes run by the Centre and state governments and the benefits available under them.“I believe that it is the BJP's responsibility to take this message of public service and dedication to the people,” Nabin said.Nabin used the announcement to contrast India’s economic position before PM Modi became Prime Minister in 2014 with the present.“When he took over the leadership of the country, India was facing policy paralysis and was being referred to as one of the 'Fragile Five' economies. Today, India is the fastest-growing major economy in the world,” he said.“There was a time when the atmosphere at that time was one of despair and darkness. Our economy was seen as part of the Fragile Five. But today, India stands out as the world's fastest-growing economy,” Nabin said.He also said India’s stature on the global stage had risen under the PM Modi-led government.Turning to young people, Nabin said PM Modi had sought to replace what he described as an atmosphere of despair with hope after 2014.“There was a time when the youth of the country were immersed in an atmosphere of despair. It was the honourable Prime Minister who, since 2014, took up the task of placing them in an environment of hope and optimism,” he said.Nabin cited the expansion of India’s startup ecosystem as part of that shift.“Through startups and unicorns, India has today become the third-largest startup nation in the world. In startups and unicorns, our youth have come forward and emerged as job givers and not just job seekers,” he said.He also referred to Khelo India and Fit India while speaking about opportunities for young people.Women-led development will also form part of the BJP’s account of PM Modi’s tenure.“The Prime Minister spoke about Women-led Development, and the journey that began under his leadership with Beti Bachao-Beti Padhao has today reached the Lakhpati Didi milestone,” Nabin said.He also referred to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam and the government’s efforts to increase women’s participation in policymaking.Nabin said the government had also sought to change the way border settlements were viewed.“There was a time when border villages were called India's last villages. They changed this perception and started calling them India's first villages. This has not only brought changes in the lives of ordinary people, but has also altered people's outlook towards these communities,” he said.Nabin traced PM Modi’s development record to Gujarat, citing work on the Narmada project and the Vibrant Gujarat initiative.“Gujarat's growth became a development model that other states could aspire to emulate,” Nabin said.He also referred to the government’s campaign against Naxalism and said PM Modi’s record should not be viewed only through economic or physical development.“Under PM Modi's leadership, India's progress has not been limited to material development; our cultural identity and heritage have also been strengthened,” he said.Nabin cited the Ram Mandir and Kashi Vishwanath while discussing the government’s emphasis on cultural heritage.“From the Ram Mandir to Kashi Vishwanath, he has worked to preserve, restore, and develop the country's rich cultural heritage,” he said.Describing PM Modi’s political journey, Nabin said, “His journey began as an ordinary party worker, and today, he has advanced the nation's progress as its 'Pradhan Sevak'. This has been made possible solely through his clear vision, firm resolve, and continuous efforts to bring about qualitative changes in society and transform lives.”PM Modi took oath as Gujarat’s 14th chief minister on October 7, 2001. He served as chief minister for nearly 13 years before moving to national politics and becoming Prime Minister in 2014.
Article Summary: Bjp to launch month-long ‘seva sankalp abhiyan’ nationwide to mark 25 years of pm modi’s parliamentary political journey. Campaign to begin on pm modi's birthday on september 17 and continue until october 17. October 7, 2026, will mark pm modi completing 25 years in public service.

Article Title: Why Vijay's gold ring scheme may miss its September 15 launch
Article Text:
Under Vijay's gold ring scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.

What is the gold ring scheme?

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's gold ring scheme, which was scheduled to be launched on September 15, shall be deferred from its expected date. The announcement comes as the CM prepares for his first official overseas visit to London. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.Vijay will leave Chennai for London via Dubai on Wednesday night and is expected to stay in the UK capital for a few days. He will travel on an Emirates Airlines passenger flight.During the visit, Vijay is expected to invite European companies to set up businesses in Tamil Nadu and seek fresh investment commitments for the state. Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London. Some may leave ahead of the chief minister to prepare for his meetings with prospective investors.The visit comes soon after the ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, where the state government announced investment commitments worth Rs 1,02,514 crore through 104 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).Security and protocol arrangements for Vijay’s departure are also being finalised.A high-level Advance Security Liaison meeting is reportedly scheduled at Chennai’s old airport on Wednesday to review the arrangements.Vijay’s London visit also comes amid key political developments in Tamil Nadu. Before leaving for the UK, he is scheduled to chair a second alliance coordination meeting at the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam headquarters in Panaiyur.The meeting is expected to discuss the structure of the ruling alliance and post-poll coalition arrangements. A Common Minimum Programme is also on the agenda, along with discussions on a steering committee and an official name for the alliance.Invitations have reportedly been sent to all alliance partners, including Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK, CPI and CPM. Congress, VCK, IUML and MDMK have confirmed their attendance, while the Left parties are likely to stay away.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election. The initiative was planned as a symbolic gift to newborns and draws on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’.Under the scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.“Through this scheme, the government assumes the role of the maaman (uncle) for every child born in its institutions, presenting a gold ring as an enduring token of welcome,” a government order said.The scheme was originally scheduled to be launched on September 15, which coincides with the birth anniversary of former chief minister C N Annadurai.It will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday. The government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of the child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover all newborns delivered at government institutions. There will be no restriction based on birth order and no gender-based discrimination.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will also be established to oversee implementation and monitoring.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries each year, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or about 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are delivered at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents such as ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was intended to combine cultural significance with public healthcare.“Gold carries profound cultural and emotional resonance in Tamil Nadu. Gifting gold to a newborn celebrates the baby’s arrival, honours the mother’s noble journey and transforms public health delivery into a source of immense community pride,” the order said.
Article Summary: Under vijay's gold ring scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around rs 13,600. Vijay is set to meet european industrialists during the visit and pitch tamil nadu as an investment destination.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday took cognisance of Greater Noida executive magistrate's notice to a 2nd year law student for participating in a protest led by Cockroach Janata Party.Though the notice was withdrawn, the apex court said that it is a serious matter as its September 1 pan-India direction barred action against students.According to the Live Law, the matter was brought to the attention of a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant."How could a magistrate dare to issue notice? We made clear no coercive action against any student! No magistrate could violate that order," CJI said.This comes a day after Allahabad high court reprimanded Noida DM Medha Roopam for imposing the National Security Act on Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary, saying that errant bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian dystopia" and reminded civil servants that their loyalty lies with the Constitution and not the political executive.A division bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev observed that bureaucrats and police officers enjoy immense powers because they are entrusted with protecting the constitutional rights, dignity and welfare of citizens."They must remember that their loyalty is towards the Constitution and not the political executive," the court said.The 15-page order, made public days after the court quashed the NSA detention and awarded Rs 5 lakh compensation to Chaudhary on Sept 2, contains sharp criticism of the Gautam Budh Nagar administration and police for invoking the stringent preventive detention law against a student activist without adequate material.Warning against abuse of authority, the bench observed that when officials disregard their constitutional oath, they risk being perceived as "an oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating conditions for civil unrest. "It shall not be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia," the court remarked.The bench was particularly critical of Gautam Budh Nagar DM Medha Roopam, who had approved the NSA detention.It held that where the police dossier contained only allegations and no credible supporting material, the district magistrate was expected to scrutinise the records threadbare before invoking the extraordinary powers available under the NSA.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026. The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.
Article Summary: The supreme court took cognisance of greater noida executive magistrate's notice to a 2nd year law student for participating in a protest led by cockroach janata party. The apex court said that it is a serious matter as its september 1 pan-india direction barred action against students.

Article Title: Building collapses to fires, 33k died in 5 years from 2020
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Between 2020 and 2024, nearly 33,000 people died across the country in incidents involving building collapses, fires and falls into pits and manholes, according to govt data. Most of these deaths occurred in urban areas, pointing to serious gaps in civic governance and enforcement of safety regulations.The actual numbers will be significantly higher as data on road deaths within municipal limits – many on account of potholes – and those due to contaminated water are unavailable.The data taken from reports of National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) show that thousands of deaths every year are linked to accidents that are largely preventable and often occur due to poor upkeep of public infrastructure, unsafe buildings and non-compliance with safety regulations. There are no specific data on deaths due to consumption of contaminated water and unhygienic conditions.While recent incidents in Delhi, including those in Satya Niketan, Hauz Rani, Palam and Vivek Vihar have caught the attention of people, instances of parts of Gurgaon and Delhi getting flooded and accumulation of piles of garbage are clear indicators of how municipal governance has deteriorated.“There is a lack of will to address the issues and no one wants to take responsibility.Every corporator or councillor, municipal officer and mayor needs to take responsibility. In every budget, mayors must inform people what they have done, where they have failed and what they would do. Accountability at each level is necessary,” said former urban development secretary M Ramachandran.PSN Rao, dean of School of Planning and Architecture, Delhi said municipal authorities only need to follow the law and enforce rules that are already laid down. “How many municipal commissioners tour different parts of cities? It’s the duty of municipal officers to carry out regular inspections to identify dangerous buildings and take necessary action. There is no alternative to strict enforcement. When there is a red signal, you must stop; else there will be an accident.It’s as simple as that,” he added.A retired civil servant who worked in the urban development ministry and in top positions in states said that there is lack of supervision and monitoring down the line. “There is adequate manpower. Across cities you will find municipal officers knocking at the door when one starts any construction work. So, there is no shortage of hands for monitoring purposes. ‘Fish rots from the head’, as the Japanese saying goes, and things must start from the top,” he said.Experts and former officials who have worked in the sector also stressed that govt’s push for ease of construction and deregulation must follow a balanced approach. “The distinction between deregulating to increase economic activity and deregulation that leads to collapse of civic order is a fine one and has been lost in the rush to deregulate everything. Officers are unable to draw the line and have stopped attending to routine work under the guise of deregulation. An important side-effect has been de-skilling as they are no longer able to decide and act,” one of them said.
Article Summary: Between 2020 and 2024, nearly 33,000 people died across the country in incidents involving building collapses, fires and falls into pits and manholes. The actual numbers will be significantly higher as data on road deaths within municipal limits – many on account of potholes – and those due to contaminated water are unavailable.

M-Seva app.The Bhagwant Mann government has extended Punjab's statewide Cleanliness Campaign 2.0 till September 12 after more than 5,400 civic complaints were resolved, Local Government Minister (GVPs).He appealed to residents to keep their waste at home until the collection vehicle arrives and warned that littering in public places would attract fines after the awareness phase.“Without active public participation, sustainable cleanliness is impossible,” Bains said, urging citizens to join the Saturday drives and spend two to three hours cleaning parks, markets and neighbourhoods.The minister said he had personally visited Kurali, Kharar and Nangal over the past 10 days to review the campaign on the ground and interact with sanitation workers.The department will conduct a detailed analysis of the campaign after September 12, including photographic evidence of garbage vulnerable points that have been permanently eliminated, Bains said.

LUCKNOW: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday highlighted the state's rich textile heritage and industrial potential, saying Uttar Pradesh has skilled manpower, a large market, industry, entrepreneurship and the world's youngest workforce.He said textiles produced in India, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, had historically been in demand in markets across the world.Addressing the two-day 'UP Textile Conclave-2026', Uttar Pradesh CM said, "In the past, the textiles that India used to produce, especially those made in Uttar Pradesh, were in demand in markets around the world, in the cultures of Rome and Greece."The Chief Minister said Varanasi's silk sarees, Bhadohi's carpets, Lucknow's chikankari, and Kanpur's textile, leather and industrial manufacturing ecosystem reflect Uttar Pradesh's rich heritage and industrial capabilities.He also highlighted the potential for technical textiles and sports goods in Meerut."Whether it's the silk sarees of Varanasi, the carpets of Bhadohi, the chikankari of Lucknow, the textile, leather and industrial manufacturing ecosystem of Kanpur, or the possibilities of technical textiles along with sports goods in Meerut, these are not just clusters of Uttar Pradesh but the heritage of Uttar Pradesh's textiles and different phases of Uttar Pradesh's industrial capability," he further said.The Chief Minister further said Uttar Pradesh has the necessary resources and ecosystem to strengthen its textile sector."We have skill, we have human resources, and we also have the country's largest market. We have industry, we have entrepreneurship, and we also have the world's youngest workforce," CM Yogi said."Over the past 6 years, there has been an increase of approximately 56 percent in the export of textiles, apparel, and handicrafts from the state," he said.He also held a meeting with leading textile and apparel entrepreneurs.The two-day UP Textile Conclave-2026 (UP-TEX 2026) is being held from September 8 to 9 at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow and was inaugurated by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi.

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday accused Aam Aadmi Party of "crushing those who question" the Punjab government after a man died by suicide following alleged pressure to apologise for publicly questioning the state's finance minister over the drug menace in the state.In a social media post on X, Rahul said Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should immediately demand his minister Harpal Singh Cheema's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation."A dangerous pattern is emerging in Punjab's AAP government - if you question government failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said."Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the finance minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologise, that he consumed poison. Wandering from one hospital to another, without access to treatment, he ultimately lost the battle for his life," he added.He said the government's job is to answer to the people, "not to crush those who ask questions"."Last week, I also spoke with a young Mohanjeet Singh, who was tortured for protesting against chief minister Bhagwant Mann," Rahul said."The government's job is to answer to the people, not to crush those who ask questions.May Gulzar Singh ji's family get justice as soon as possible. The chief minister should immediately demand the finance minister's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation, with his name registered in the FIR," he added.A controversy erupted after a 47-year-old man, Gulzar Singh, from Sangrur allegedly died by suicide, with his family claiming that he was asked to apologise and subjected to casteist slurs for questioning finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the "unabated" supply of 'chitta' in his area at an event on September 6.Singh died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison, his family members said.A purported video of Gulzar's last moments surfaced in which he spoke about questioning the finance minister, prompting opposition parties to demand the resignations of Cheema as well as Mann.Punjab Police set up a special investigation team (SIT), led by an officer of additional director general of police rank, in connection with the suicide incident.Following a complaint by Gulzar's family, five villagers - Baljit Singh, Sukhdev Singh, Vicky Singh, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur - have been booked under Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and relevant sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, according to the FIR.

NEW DELHI: Amruta Fadnavis , wife of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , said there was nothing wrong with Muslims participating in Navratri and other festivals, after the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for Muslims to be barred from the upcoming Navratri festivities, a demand endorsed by state minister Nitesh Rane.“Festivals are inclusive, and there is nothing wrong with a Muslim person attending the celebrations. Article Text:
BJP got Rs 1,473cr to fight Bengal, Assam, 3 other assembly polls

NEW DELHI: Total receipts by BJP's central party headquarters during the last round of assembly polls in Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry stood at Rs 1,472.8 crore, as per the party's election expenditure statements for Assam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry submitted to the Election Commission.The party's closing balance rose to Rs 7,627.2 crore upon the completion of elections on May 6, 2026, compared to Rs 6,722.6 crore on March 15, 2026.BJP, including the party's central headquarters and the relevant state and district units, spent a total Rs 160 crore on the assembly elections in Assam, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Assam accounted for the BJP's highest spend at Rs 96.3 crore, followed by TN at Rs 51.6 crore and Puducherry (Rs 11.9 crore). Almost Rs 130.4 crore was spent on general party propaganda, while Rs 29.6 crore went to candidates as lump sum payments and on the publicity of their criminal antecedents. The election expenditure statements for the other two states of West Bengal and Kerala are yet to be made public by EC.As per BJP's election expenditure statements for Assam, the party spent Rs 76.7 crore on general party propaganda, which included Rs 23.1 crore spent by its central unit, and another Rs 19.5 crore spent on candidates.While Rs 27.3 crore was spent on travel expenses of star campaigners in Assam, Rs 37 crore was on advertisements, Rs 8.9 crore on publicity materials and Rs 2.3 crore on other expenses by the state unit. A total lump sum of Rs 19.4 crore was paid to candidates and Rs 16.7 lakh spent on publishing criminal antecedents of candidates. In TN, BJP authorised a total spend of Rs 44.5 crore for general party propaganda. Another Rs 7 crore was spent on candidates.In its expenditure statement released earlier for the same set of elections, Congress had declared a total spend of Rs 248.6 crore.
Article Summary: Bjp got rs 1,473cr to fight bengal, assam, 3 other assembly polls. Assam accounted for the bjp's highest spend at rs 96.3 crore, followed by tn at rs 51.6 crore and puducherry. Almost rs 130.4 crore was spent on general party propaganda.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday renewed his "naraz fufa" jibe at the Congress, saying "some people could never be happy with India's progress."The Prime Minister received an enthusiastic welcome at the ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat’ event, with organisers saying all seats were booked within an hour of online ticket sales opening.The programme featured music and cultural performances, including a rendition of Queen’s ‘We Will Rock You’, as the crowd cheered for the PM.Addressing the 'NaMo for Viksit Bharat' event in Vadodara, PM Modi highlighted the capacity of India’s dedicated freight corridors while taking a dig at the Congress by referring them as "naraaz fufa"."Recently, a double-stack container freight train was operated from JNPT (Mumbai) to Vadodara—meaning the train ran with one container stacked on top of another," he said."With this single trip, the volume of cargo transported from Mumbai to Vadodara was equivalent to that of over 250 trucks. Now, enter the 'naraaz fufa' figure—the one who will immediately start complaining: "What about the truck drivers? Where will the trucks go? What will happen to those who bought trucks?" Well, 'fufa' has found something to grumble about now..." he added.PM Modi said the freight corridor would reduce travel time and logistics costs while saving fuel and benefiting the environment.“Today, the work on the 2,800-kilometer corridor has been successfully completed. The Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors are now becoming the backbone of the nation's trade and commerce,” he said.The Prime Minister also credited his government with speeding up the freight corridor project after 2014, while criticising the previous government for delays."In 2014, the people of Vadodara, Gujarat, and the entire nation sent me from Gujarat to Delhi. The previous government remained in power until 2014; you sent me there, and they were shown the door. In 7-8 years, not even a single kilometer of work on the freight corridor had been completed. Had the country been run according to their methods, who knows—even three or four subsequent generations might have passed without it ever getting done. That was the state in which they had left a project meant to transform India's logistics ecosystem. After 2014, I set about accelerating this work immediately."The Prime Minister said the project had transformed the country's logistics system and reflected a change in work culture."This Dedicated Freight Corridor stands as a testament to how the country's work culture has transformed over the last 12 years. The concept for this Dedicated Freight Corridor was first mooted in 2004... A special company was formed in 2006 to execute this project. Yet, until 2014, the files merely shuttled back and forth; they were just traveling from one table to another. And look at the irony—even these files did not get the benefit of a dedicated corridor. .." he added.The ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat Vadodara’ programme was organised as part of PM Modi's visit to the city, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for various development projects.Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi said the programme had received an overwhelming response from residents. For the first time, online ticketing was introduced, with all available seats booked within 60 minutes. Demand was reportedly three times higher than the available capacity.Special fan zones were also set up to accommodate people who could not get seats inside the venue.Ahead of PM Modi’s visit, a ‘Viksit Bharat Padayatra’ was organised on Monday under Sanghavi’s leadership. The march began at the Faculty of Technology in Dandia Bazaar and passed through Kirti Stambh before concluding at Sursagar Lake.A cultural programme was also organised at Sursagar Lake, featuring singer Kailash Kher. ‘Swachhata Doots’ who contributed to keeping Vadodara clean were felicitated during the event.During his visit, PM Modi inaugurated, dedicated and laid the foundation stones for development projects worth more than Rs 35,000 crore in Vadodara.A major highlight was the inauguration of three sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore.The sections connect New Sanand (North) with New Makarpura, New Umbergaon with New Saphale, and New Saphale with New JNPT in Mumbai. The connectivity to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority is expected to speed up the movement of export-import cargo, improve links between industrial centres and ports and reduce logistics costs.PM Modi also flagged off freight train services from the newly connected sections and a new passenger train between Tanda Road and Vadodara’s Pratapnagar.He dedicated the Jobat-Tanda Road new rail line to the nation. The line, developed as part of the Chhota Udepur-Dhar project, will connect remote and tribal areas of Alirajpur with the national railway network.The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for three railway projects covering 329 km at a cost of more than Rs 9,700 crore, along with three National Highway projects worth around Rs 1,780 crore.Several Gujarat government projects worth around Rs 2,600 crore were also inaugurated or launched, including housing projects under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, a water-supply project for 11 villages in eastern Vadodara, the Vadodara Urban Development Authority Ring Road Phase II and a 110 MW floating solar project at Kadana Dam.

NEW DELHI: The Congress ' West Bengal unit on Tuesday lodged a police complaint against Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent “avoid non-veg during Durga Puja” remark, asserting that the call was “intended to create disharmony. ”In the complaint submitted to the officer-in-charge of Kolkata’s Bhawanipore police station, the South Kolkata District Congress Committee alleged that Shastri made “derogatory” comments during an event in Howrah on September 5.“We want to apprise you that immediate administrative action needs to be initiated, and an FIR needs to be registered with necessary arrests. Eiffel Tower in Paris was closed to visitors Monday after staff suddenly went on strike, alleging that female employees were moved from their stations during a visit by a delegation from a Gujarat-based Hindu religious group.A 100-strong delegation linked to Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) had visited Eiffel Tower ahead of Festival of Cultures, marking the consecration of a Swaminarayan Temple in Paris over the weekend.PTI quoted workers' union representative Diane Davoine as saying women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark. Confederation Generale du Travail, a national forum of trade unions, alleged that in some cases, women employees were temporarily replaced by male colleagues and told to avoid particular areas till the religious delegation left.The operating company, Societe d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), said the tower reopened as usual on Tuesday, acknowledging that a BAPS delegation had requested "limited interactions with women" and that the condition "should not have been accepted".BAPS issued a detailed statement insisting the arrangements were never gender-based. It said the visit was coordinated in advance purely for logistical reasons."Given the size of the group, this visit was coordinated in advance with the Eiffel Tower's management team and was scheduled at the start of normal operating hours specifically to minimise any disruption to staff, other visitors, and the site's regular functioning." MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the matter was purely between the entities concerned.BAPS regretted any inconvenience caused to employees by the arrangements. "We take seriously the concerns expressed by the Eiffel Tower's employees, and we sincerely regret any inconvenience or discomfort caused to them as a result of the arrangements made for our group's visit."Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire called the employees' anger legitimate. National Assembly President Yael Braun-Pivet said women in France fully occupy public spaces and cannot be told to make themselves invisible. Gender equality minister Aurore Berge called the episode unacceptable, saying no religion is above the Republic's laws. Former PM Gabriel Attal backed Tower's staff, saying no culture or belief can dictate a woman's place.
Article Summary: Eiffel tower in paris was closed to visitors monday after staff suddenly went on strike. Workers' union representative diane davoine said women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark.

Article Title: Channi vs Warring: Why Sachin Pilot may be Congress's best bet in Punjab
Article Text:
Congress has handed Sachin Pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity.

Why Congress was forced to budge

Bhupesh Baghel had asserted that it is not a 'child's play' and the decision of the high command will not change.

Why Sachin Pilot

Punjab Congress working president welcomed Sachin Pilot’s appointment, saying it will help iron out differences within the state unit.

Baghel gone. Will Warring be next?

Congress has a lot at stake

Punjab could shape Pilot's Rajasthan future

NEW DELHI: The Congress leadership last week finally responded to 'Mayday' calls from Punjab rebels and brought in Sachin Pilot , replacing Bhupesh Baghel , to prevent a crash landing of the deeply fractured state unit ahead of the assembly elections early next year.Months of open infighting between Charanjit Singh Channi, the former chief minister leading the rebel camp, and Raja Warring, the state unit chief, not just embarrassed the Congress but also threatened to derail its 2027 campaign.Before being put in the driver's seat in Punjab, Pilot was in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel remains a key Congress leader and former chief minister.The Congress had sent former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhagel to Punjab in February this year to defuse the brewing Channi vs Warring crisis in the state unit. Ironically, as things turned out, Baghel faced resistance and became part of the crisis, with the Channi camp openly accusing him of siding with Warring. More so, since July, after the party’s central leadership decided to ignore Channi’s claim for the top post in the state and announced that it would continue with Warring as state Congress president.With several senior state leaders backing Channi, the fight turned ugly and Baghel became ineffective.Congress meetings in the districts saw open “Go back Baghel” chants from Channi supporters, taking the infighting to the streets and embarrassing the top leadership.So, while the ruling Aam Aadmi Party was already in full election mode with chief minister Bhagwant Mann at the centre of its campaign, the Congress was still struggling to get its senior leadership to sit across the table.Not just the AAP, even the BJP and the Akalis had their house in order and were planning their electoral moves on the ground. With the party's 2027 campaign failing to take off under Baghel, the Congress was forced to budge and turn to Pilot.The Congress decision to send Pilot to Punjab, while ironic, may still be the best bet for the leadership. Sachin Pilot, during his years in the Congress, has seen enough internal wars to know how quickly a fight over one post can turn into a larger battle over leadership, political space and, of course, eventually the chief minister's chair.Throwback to Rajasthan, where he spent years at the centre of a similar leadership tussle with senior leader Ashok Gehlot. Pilot brings something the Congress needs badly right now: the experience of being at the centre of a difficult internal power struggle.Pilot has led the Rajasthan unit, worked closely with the high command, weathered the bitter internal battle, survived the fallout and then rebuilt his position within the Congress.He was appointed Rajasthan Congress chief in 2014, after the party's abysmal performance in the 2013 assembly election. Over the next four years, he emerged as one of the key faces of the party's rebuilding effort before Congress returned to power in 2018. That victory, however, did not give him the chief minister's chair.Ashok Gehlot became chief minister, while Pilot was made deputy chief minister and continued as PCC president. While both sides got something, the arrangement never really settled the rivalry between Gehlot and Pilot.By 2020, those differences exploded into an open rebellion.Pilot left Jaipur with a group of MLAs and challenged the Gehlot government. Congress responded by removing him as deputy chief minister and state president. The Gehlot camp even accused him of working with the BJP. A truce was eventually worked out, and Pilot stayed with Congress.But he never quite returned to the position he had occupied before and has been on the sidelines ever since. He remained a prominent face in the party and was later given charge of Chhattisgarh, but his role in Rajasthan remained limited.It is interesting how, in Rajasthan, Pilot was the leader asking the Congress high command to listen to a dissatisfied camp. In Punjab, he now has to convince dissatisfied leaders to accept the high command's decisions and work together.That may be why Congress believes he is best suited for the job.But will Pilot’s appointment end the crisis in the Punjab unit?Channi's supporters had demanded Warring be removed as Punjab Congress chief, and the Jalandhar MP be declared Congress’s chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly polls. The Congress has not accepted either of the two demands. So, while Channi has not made any significant gains, Warring has been left wondering if he will be the next to be axed.Warring was picked up to lead and rebuild the Punjab unit after the Congress was decimated in the 2022 assembly polls. Channi, who was the chief minister then, led the Congress to its worst-ever performance in the state. The Congress not just lost its government to AAP but was also reduced to 18 seats in the 117-member assembly.The leadership tussle between the two had been brewing for quite some time. But as is the Congress’s wont, the party kept dilly-dallying on the issue for nearly 4 years. Finally, when the Congress did take a decision, it ended up opening deep faultlines.For now, both camps have welcomed his appointment. Warring said Pilot's energy and dynamism would "for sure" add to the vigour of the party ahead of the crucial polls, while Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, a close associate of Channi, said Pilot's experience, leadership and connect with the people would give new strength and momentum to the Congress in Punjab.Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka hopes that under Pilot’s leadership all state leaders would come together. "Pilot knows all leaders of Punjab, and they also have confidence in him," said Verka.For Pilot, this may be his first real test. If party leadership decides to keep Warring, he has to get Channi, Randhawa and other leaders to fall in line. If Warring goes, he has to make sure one problem is not replaced by the other.The Congress, which remains the main challenger for now, cannot afford this infighting because Punjab is one of the states where it still has a real chance. There is anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government.In 2022, AAP swept 92 of the 117 assembly seats, while Congress was reduced to 18. But the 2024 Lok Sabha election brought some relief for the grand old party. The Congress won seven of Punjab's 13 seats, compared with AAP's three, showing that the party still has enough ground to be a serious challenger.AAP is perhaps no longer riding the wave that brought it to power in 2022 and is now defending its record under Bhagwant Mann. Raghav Chadha's exit has also added to the churn in the party.The BJP and the Akalis are still on the margins of the state’s politics. But the scenario could change very fast. The BJP is going all out to broaden its organisational base and rope in leaders from other parties. There are also reports of talks between the BJP and the Akalis to revive their old alliance. The Congress needs to remember that the BJP is coming off a massive victory in West Bengal and is looking to expand its footprint in Punjab as well.Pilot has already made it clear that he sees Punjab as a comeback opportunity for the Congress. On Monday, he said he was confident that with a strong organisation, collective effort and the energy of party workers, Congress could return to power in the state.Pilot has the experience of being a part of successful strategising in Himachal Pradesh in the previous assembly polls and has also been a senior observer for the Kerala polls, where Congress returned to power after a decade.If Pilot can manage to bring the rival Punjab camps together and help the Congress put up a strong show in 2027, it will add to his standing within the party at a time when Rajasthan is already looking ahead to the 2028 assembly election.There has long been speculation over a bigger role for Pilot in Rajasthan. He may not have got it yet, but a successful Punjab stint could considerably strengthen his case.For a leader who has had to rebuild his own position in the party before, Punjab could well become the next big step in that comeback.
Article Summary: Congress has handed sachin pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity. Why congress was forced to budge in punjab. Pilot brings something the congress needs badly right now: the experience of being at the centre of a difficult internal power struggle. Pilot was the leader asking the congress high command to listen to a dissatisfied camp.

NEW DELHI: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta , who served during chief minister Sheila Dikshit ’s tenure, allegedly died by suicide at his residence in Noida, officials said on Tuesday.Mehta, 74, a 1975-batch IAS officer, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at his Sector 82 residence on September 6, officials told news agency PTI.Noida Police recovered a purported suicide note in which he cited his "mental and health issues" as the reasons behind the extreme step.Mehta's body was cremated at the Lodhi Road crematorium on Monday.Mehta served as Delhi's chief secretary for more than three years, taking charge in 2007 and retiring in November 2010. Article Title: Village head's appeal drove Ladakh LG's initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation
Article Text:
Village head’s appeal drove Ladakh LG’s initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation

SRINAGAR: Nearly 90 million litres of glacial water have started irrigating more than 1,000 acres of parched farmlands across 12 villages in Ladakh every day, thanks to a pioneering initiative by lieutenant governor (LG) V K Saxena last month.The massive volume of glacier-melt, previously flowing untapped into the River Indus, is now being channelised from Stok village nallah in Leh into the Igoo-Phey Irrigation Canal using simple earthwork that incurred little capital expenditure.It was an appeal from a village chief that drove the LG to brainstorm on harnessing glaciers and snowmelt for productive use. According to officials, Saxena was on a visit to Chuchot village in Leh where the ‘goba’ (or nambardar, the traditional village head), Mirza Hussain, sought his intervention to address the acute water shortage in the village.The plea prompted the LG to spearhead a comprehensive and systematic campaign to identify locations where large volumes of glacial water were flowing down unused, draining straight into the Indus, even as surrounding farmlands remained dry, officials said.The govt first identified Stok village nallah, fed by the Stok Kangri Glacier, as one such place where glacier water could be diverted into the existing canal.Officials said the discharge from Stok nallah was assessed at 36 cusecs, or approximately 90 million litres of water in 24 hours.Two channels were then created to divert nearly 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal — 62 million litres toward Igoo village upstream and approximately 18 million litres toward Phey village downstream.This daily flow has substantially augmented the total water flow in the Igoo-Phey Canal — from 50 cusecs to nearly 90 cusecs. As a result, water supply will be guaranteed daily to the 12 villages fed by the canal. Previously, water from the 43-km-long Igoo-Phey Canal was distributed to villages on a restrictive roster basis due to limited availability.Having successfully channelised 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal, the remaining 10 million litres were diverted into another dry canal at Chuchot, and will help irrigate farmland in and around the village, officials said.“The entire 90 million litres of water was tapped and the discharge from Stok Kangri glacier into the Indus River was reduced to zero in just two days at no cost,” said an official, adding that the success of the initiative serves as a blueprint for water management across the Union Territory.
Article Summary: Village head's appeal drove ladakh lg’s initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation. The massive volume of glacier-melt is now being channelised from stok village nallah in leh into the igoo-phey irrigation canal.

Article Title: 'You can't keep it lingering': Supreme Court to Odisha on Dara Singh plea
Article Text:
‘You can’t keep it lingering’: SC

NEW DELHI: Pulling up Odisha govt over its indecisiveness on taking a call on the remission plea of Dara Singh, SC Tuesday said the state cannot linger on the issue and made it clear that the official (secretary) concerned will be summoned if decision is not taken by Sept 17, the next date of hearing.A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi expressed displeasure after Odisha govt sought a four-week adjournment on the ground of illness of its advocate-on-record (AoR). Deferring the hearing, the court made it clear that no adjournment will be granted on the next date. "You cannot keep it lingering like this. Take a decision, accept or reject. You cannot avoid taking decision," the bench said.Noting that hearing in the case had been adjourned multiple times to allow the state to take a call on the remission plea, the court at the previous hearing also expressed displeasure over State Sentence Review Board not having made a decision yet. SC made it clear to state govt that it would have to pass an order if the authority did not make a decision.

NEW DELHI: The NIA has not invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in its chargesheet against six Ukrainian nationals and a US citizen in a case registered under the anti-terror law in April. The chargesheet instead invokes sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.The chargesheet said the accused had valid travel documents but didn't obtain the mandatory Protected Area Permit (PAP) required to enter Mizoram. Special judge Prashant Sharma will consider the chargesheet on Oct 1.American citizen VanDyke and Ukrainian nationals Kaminskyi Viktor, Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian, and Honcharuk Maksim were arrested in March at various airports for allegedly travelling to Mizoram without the required permits and crossing into Myanmar.An FIR was registered against them under UAPA over their suspected links to armed groups in Myanmar, where multiple militant organisations active in North-East India maintain bases.Earlier, NIA had told the court that the foreigners were being probed for a wider terror conspiracy, including allegedly assisting ethnic armed groups in India and Myanmar and imparting drone training to them.The chargesheet traced their movement from India to Myanmar from Dec 2025. Article Summary: The nia has not invoked the unlawful activities (prevention) act (uapa) in its chargesheet against six ukrainian nationals and a us citizen. The chargesheet instead invokes sections 21 and 23 of the immigration and foreigners act, 2025. An fir was registered against them under uapa over their suspected links to armed groups in myanmar.
